Windows may show a "protected your PC" notice the first time because the file is new and not yet widely downloaded. Open the zip, then run RubyClient.exe. Choose More info, then Run anyway. Needs the free .NET 9 Desktop Runtime.

What it is

A hub of apps and a browser, in one window.

RubyClient is a desktop program. Open it and you get a list of apps: a web browser, game demos, a clip maker, web apps like Discord and Steam, and a set of everyday tools.

Ruby BrowserClip StudioGame DemosAccountsWeatherDiscordSteamClipboard historyNotesTasksCalculatorConverterFocus TimerPassword makerSecure VaultQR StudioToolboxWorld ClockPC SpecsLive MonitorDisk AnalyzerBulk RenamerNetwork ToolsAutoclicker
How it works

Three steps. That is all.

01

Download

Download RubyClient. It is one file; there is no installer to click through.

02

Double-click

Open it and choose an app from the list on the left. The Ruby Browser opens in its own window with the tab rail on the side.

03

It keeps itself up to date

Updates are checked when Ruby starts and installed by themselves. Every update is signed, and a damaged or fake file is refused.

Windows needs the free .NET 9 Desktop Runtime and Microsoft WebView2 (both are already on most PCs; Windows will offer them if not).

Benefits

Why people use it

A browser that is yours

Tabs sit on a ruby rail at the side. Full history you can search, private windows that leave nothing behind, and a tracker blocker.

Ruby VPN, one switch

Turn it on, pick a country. Nothing to install or log into. It runs through Tor, so it is slower than a normal VPN, and covers the Ruby browser only.

Tor engine tabs

Switch a tab to the Tor engine for extra privacy. Needs the Tor Browser installed once.

Everything in one place

Notes, a calculator, a clip maker, a vault and more, so you are not hunting for a dozen separate programs.

Light on your PC

A memory limiter, and animations that stop when the window is hidden, keep it quiet in the background.

Looks like nothing else

Ruby colours, faceted gem tiles, and themes and wallpapers you can change in settings.

Founder

Peter Medvediev

Peter founded RubyClient and leads its design and development. The idea is simple: your everyday tools and your browser should feel like one well-made thing, look good, and respect your privacy.
